audit.whatIsWrong: Level 6, First item and Two+ items all read Skill. The already-audited mirror sets Levels 1 through 6 to Sylas and both item rows to Dr. Mundo, and the packet agrees on Level 6 and Two+ items.
audit.why: Level 6 is the clearest window in the lane — you deny Maximum Dosage and gain the chase speed — while at two items his health stacking and regeneration put the duel out of reach. Calling both 'Skill' hides the two moments that decide the matchup.
audit.corrected: Level 6 reads Sylas at 7/10, First item and Two+ items read Dr. Mundo.

audit.whatIsWrong: The mid text gives Heart Zapper an 11-second cooldown.
audit.why: It is 17/16.5/16/15.5/15s — never below 15. A player told to expect it back in 11 seconds will hold off for a window that has already been open for four, and will step in expecting it down when it is up.
audit.corrected: Stated as 15-17s in mid, the cooldown breakdown and dosFull[0].d, with Maximum Dosage's flat 120s against your Hijack at 80/55/30s.

audit.whatIsWrong: Goes Where He Pleases is described only as 'passive regeneration'. Riot's text has it resist the first immobilizing effect that hits him, dropping a cannister he can walk over to heal and lower its cooldown. Blunt Force Trauma's auto-attack reset is also never given as the burst tell.
audit.why: The CC resist matters directly to Sylas: a Hijacked ultimate with hard CC in it gets eaten by the passive rather than landing, and the cannister on the ground is a heal you can deny by fighting away from it. The E reset is the wind-up that tells you to step out.
audit.corrected: Cannister and CC-resist named in whys[0] and wants.foe[1]; the Blunt Force Trauma wind-up named as the step-back cue in mid.

audit.whatIsWrong: The entry has Grievous Wounds in the right places but never says that resistances are the wrong purchase against Maximum Dosage.
audit.why: His R heals a percent of missing health and then regenerates a portion of max health — armour and MR do not touch either number, which is why anti-heal timing, not stat stacking, is the answer.
The packet flags wants.you[1] 'Heart Zapper's' as a suspect name. False positive — it is the real W, in the possessive.

edits.before: - Dr. Mundo Heart Zapper: matchup-defining — His burst + sustain window — trade just after he wastes it. Count it out loud if you must. - Your E1 shield has one job: the moment it all goes wrong. - The R has one too: the moment it all goes right.
edits.after: - Dr. Mundo Heart Zapper: matchup-defining — his burst-and-heal window on 15-17s; trade just after it pops. - Maximum Dosage is a flat 120s against your 80s Hijack — never ult first. - His passive eats the first immobilise and drops a cannister; fight away from it.

edits.after: His burst-and-heal window, 15-17s — trade just after it pops. Bait it, count it, then go.

edits.after: Track Dr. Mundo’s Heart Zapper: a 15-17s burst-and-heal window — trade just after it pops. It’s down or you don’t go.

edits.after: Fully itemised Maximum Dosage heals a percent of missing health, so resistances change nothing and only Grievous Wounds does — your mid-game lead must already be cashed into objectives before this.

edits.before: Level 2 is your first real window — E in, W immediately for the missing-HP amp, and weave passive autos between spell casts to proc Petricite Burst in the chain spin. The key read is Heart Zapper: his W is an 11-second cooldown that bursts and heals him; if you hook in while it's active he absorbs your Q damage and wins the trade. Bait it, let it pop or expire, then commit. Levels 4-5 he starts itemizing toward health and his cleaver range becomes more oppressive — respect his Q angles, freeze or slow-push to deny his farm, and don't burn both E charges to initiate or you're stuck in melee with no escape if jungle collapses.
edits.after: Level 2 is your first real window — E in, W immediately for the heal, and weave autos between casts to spend Petricite Burst. The key read is Heart Zapper: 15-17s, never lower, and it both damages and stores what you deal to heal him back, so hooking in while it is live hands him the trade. Bait it, let it pop, then commit. His Blunt Force Trauma opens with an attack reset — that wind-up, not the cast, is your cue to step out. Levels 4-5 he itemises health and the cleaver gets oppressive: respect his Q angles, freeze or slow-push to deny farm, and never spend both E charges to initiate.

edits.before: At 6 this lane swings your way temporarily — if he uses Maximum Dosage to survive a trade or back you off, immediately Hijack it: you deny his survival tool and gain a speed-buffed chase R that lets you run him down before he regenerates. Force the all-in on his R cooldown, not into it. From first item onward the race tightens: Riftmaker stacks help you through long trades, but you must have Grievous Wounds — Morellonomicon or an anti-heal component — active before his R fires in teamfights or he simply heals through everything you do. By 2+ items a full Dr. Mundo becomes nearly unkillable without coordinated burst; your job is to have snowballed a kill advantage or tower lead in the mid-game window before his passive regeneration and item HP make the 1v1 unwinnable.
edits.after: At 6 the lane is yours: if he spends Maximum Dosage to survive a trade, Hijack it — you deny the save and gain the speed to run him down while his own copy sits on a flat 120s against your 80s. Force the all-in on his R cooldown, never into it. From first item the race tightens: Riftmaker carries you through long trades, but Grievous Wounds must be live before his R fires or the missing-health heal undoes the whole fight, and no amount of armour or MR touches it. By 2+ items a full Dr. Mundo is nearly unkillable without coordinated burst; the lead has to be cashed into objectives before then. Play the side lane for pressure rather than the kill, take the fight only when your team can collapse with you, and keep stealing whichever enemy ultimate wins the teamfight outright.

notes: The 11-second Heart Zapper figure was the worst error here — the real floor is 15s, so the entry's central 'bait it and commit' instruction was being timed against a cooldown four seconds shorter than reality. Goes Where He Pleases was described only as regeneration; the first-immobilise resist and the cannister pickup were absent, and both matter to Sylas specifically because a Hijacked hard-CC ultimate gets spent on the passive rather than landing.
